title: Tamil Nadu Records Highest-Ever Power Demand in July 2026 as Heatwave Drives Electricity Consumption - LiveChennai
full_text:
Tamil Nadu witnessed a record-breaking surge in electricity demand during July 2026, with the State registering its highest-ever peak power demand and daily energy consumption due to prolonged heat, unusually warm nights, and a weak southwest monsoon.
According to official data, peak power demand touched an all-time high of 21,724 MW on July 14, while daily electricity consumption reached a record 475.447 million units (MU) on July 17. The State`s total electricity consumption for July increased to 13,807 MU, up 11.5% from 12,382 MU recorded during the same month in 2025.
Heatwave and Weak Monsoon Increase Power Consumption
Weather experts said July 2026 was the second warmest July in Tamil Nadu in more than 30 years. Above-normal daytime temperatures, persistently warm nights, and high humidity forced households, businesses, and industries to use air conditioners, refrigerators, fans, and other cooling appliances for longer hours.
As a result, electricity demand remained consistently high throughout the month. Daily power consumption crossed 400 MU on 30 of the 31 days, while it exceeded 450 MU on 14 days. Peak power demand also crossed 20,000 MW on 26 days, highlighting the sustained increase in electricity usage across the State.
Demand Exceeds Official Estimates
Tamil Nadu`s actual electricity demand surpassed projections made in the Load Generation Balance Report, which had estimated a peak demand of 20,619 MW and a monthly energy requirement of 13,193 MU. However, the State recorded 21,724 MW in peak demand and 13,807 MU in monthly electricity consumption.
Renewable Energy Helps Maintain Stable Power Supply
Despite the unprecedented demand, the Tamil Nadu Power Distribution Corporation Limited (TNPDCL) successfully maintained uninterrupted power supply across the State. Officials attributed the stable electricity supply to robust wind and solar power generation, along with efficient grid management.
The record demand reflects Tamil Nadu`s growing electricity requirements and highlights the increasing importance of renewable energy in supporting the State`s expanding residential, commercial, and industrial power needs.
